raw_text:
# 3-Week Post-Illness Reconditioning Block

**Client:** 41 M, intermediate | **Pre-illness:** Bench 100 / Squat 140 / Deadlift 170 | **Context:** 3 weeks off with flu, fatigue, -4 kg

## Before You Start: Clearance and Red Flags

Flu has a small but real association with myocarditis, and returning too hard too soon is the main risk at this stage. Before session one, confirm he has been **fever-free for at least 7 days without medication** and that his fatigue is improving, not plateaued or worsening.

**Stop training and refer him to his GP** if he reports any of the following during or after sessions:
- Chest pain or tightness
- Palpitations or irregular heartbeat
- Breathlessness out of proportion to effort
- Dizziness or fainting
- A crash in energy 24–48 hours after a session (post-exertional malaise)

Because he's still reporting fatigue, a quick GP check before loading up is reasonable, especially at 41. It costs little and protects you both.

**Daily monitoring:**
- **Morning resting heart rate.** If it's more than 5–7 bpm above his baseline, run a lighter session or rest.
- **Readiness score (1–10)** for sleep, energy, and soreness. If it's 4 or below, drop the top sets that day.

## Setting Expectations

Three weeks off causes very little true strength loss in an intermediate lifter. Most of the dip is neural rust, fatigue, and lost glycogen and water. Some of the 4 kg will be muscle, though, and he is still recovering. A realistic target is **95–100% of previous working capacity by end of week 3**. Full 1RMs may take another 1–3 weeks. The block is built to autoregulate: if he's flying, the RPE caps let him push; if he's dragging, they hold him back.

## Structure

- **Frequency:** 3 sessions/week, full body, on non-consecutive days (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)
- **Session length:** 50–65 minutes
- **Autoregulation:** Every working set has an RPE cap. The percentages are starting points, and the RPE overrides them.
- **Conditioning:** Light zone 2 only (conversational pace). No HIIT in this block.

---

## Week 1: Re-Groove (RPE 6, ~60–65%)

**Goal:** Restore movement patterns, assess tolerance, and finish every session feeling better than he started. Leave 4+ reps in the tank on everything.

**Day A**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 3 × 6 | 85–90 kg |
| Bench Press | 3 × 6 | 60–65 kg |
| Chest-Supported Row | 3 × 10 | RPE 6 |
| Walking Lunge | 2 × 8/leg | Light DBs |
| Plank | 2 × 30 s | — |

**Day B**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 8 | 80–90 kg |
| Seated DB Shoulder Press | 3 × 10 | RPE 6 |
| Lat Pulldown | 3 × 10 | RPE 6 |
| Leg Press | 2 × 12 | RPE 6 |
| Face Pull | 2 × 15 | Light |

**Day C**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional Deadlift | 3 × 5 | 100–110 kg |
| Incline DB Press | 3 × 10 | RPE 6 |
| Seated Cable Row | 3 × 10 | RPE 6 |
| Goblet Squat | 2 × 10 | Moderate |
| Dead Bug | 2 × 8/side | — |

**Conditioning:** Two sessions of 15–20 minutes of zone 2 (bike or incline walk) on off days, or after lifting if he feels good.

**Progression check:** If all sessions felt easy with no next-day crash and stable resting HR, proceed. If not, repeat Week 1.

---

## Week 2: Rebuild (RPE 7, ~70–80%)

**Goal:** Restore work capacity and add volume. Main lifts move into strength rep ranges.

**Day A**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 4 × 5 | 100–110 kg |
| Bench Press | 4 × 5 | 72.5–77.5 kg |
| Chest-Supported Row | 3 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 × 8/leg | DBs |
| Hanging Knee Raise | 3 × 10 | — |

**Day B**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 6 | 100–110 kg |
| Standing Barbell OHP | 3 × 6 | RPE 7 |
| Weighted Pull-up / Pulldown | 3 × 6–8 | RPE 7 |
| Close-Grip Bench | 3 × 8 | 60–65 kg |
| Face Pull | 3 × 15 | — |

**Day C**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional Deadlift | 4 × 4 | 125–135 kg |
| Bench Press (volume) | 3 × 8 | 65–70 kg |
| Barbell Row | 3 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Front Squat | 3 × 6 | 70–80 kg |
| Pallof Press | 3 × 10/side | — |

**Conditioning:** Two to three sessions of 20–25 minutes of zone 2.

**Progression check:** Bar speed on the top sets should look close to normal. If RPE is creeping to 8+ at these loads, hold the weights for Week 3 rather than jumping.

---

## Week 3: Return to Intensity (RPE 8, ~82–90%)

**Goal:** Heavy singles and doubles to re-establish top-end strength, finishing with a rep-max estimate rather than a true 1RM test.

**Day A**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 1 × 2 @ RPE 8, then 3 × 4 | ~120–125 kg, back-offs ~110 kg |
| Bench Press | 1 × 2 @ RPE 8, then 3 × 4 | ~85–87.5 kg, back-offs ~80 kg |
| Chest-Supported Row | 3 × 8 | RPE 7–8 |
| Walking Lunge | 2 × 10/leg | Moderate |

**Day B (lighter, recovery-focused)**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 6 | 110 kg |
| Standing OHP | 3 × 5 | RPE 7 |
| Pull-ups | 3 × AMRAP −2 | — |
| Leg Press | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Face Pull | 3 × 15 | — |

**Day C: Strength Check**

Work up to a **top set of 3 @ RPE 8–9** on each lift and estimate the 1RM from it.

| Lift | Top Triple Target | Estimated 1RM if Achieved |
|---|---|---|
| Squat | 125–130 kg | ~135–140 kg |
| Bench | 90–92.5 kg | ~95–100 kg |
| Deadlift | 152.5–160 kg | ~165–170 kg |

Run the lifts in this order: squat, bench, deadlift. Use full warm-ups and rest 3–4 minutes between heavy sets. Finish with light accessories only.

**Conditioning:** Two sessions of 25–30 minutes of zone 2. You can add a few short tempo intervals if he's fully recovered.

---

## Nutrition

The 4 kg loss is the main lever here. Aim to recover 2–3 kg across the block, mostly lean tissue, glycogen, and water.

- **Calories:** Maintenance plus 300–400 kcal/day
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, spread across 4 feedings of 30–50 g each
- **Carbohydrates:** Prioritise them around training (3–5 g/kg/day) to restore glycogen and support energy
- **Hydration:** At least 35 ml/kg/day, plus electrolytes on training days
- **Micronutrients:** Encourage plenty of fruit and vegetables. If his diet is poor, a vitamin D check is reasonable at his GP visit.
- **Creatine:** If he doesn't already take it, 3–5 g/day helps restore cell hydration and strength.
- **Weekly weigh-ins:** Same day, same time, first thing in the morning

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours. This matters more than anything else during post-viral recovery.
- **Off days:** Walking (7–10k steps), mobility work, nothing exhaustive
- **Stress:** At 41 with likely work and family load, ask about his life stress weekly and adjust training volume to match.

## After Week 3

- **On target:** Move into a normal intermediate block, such as a 4-week accumulation phase. Run a true 1RM test 2–4 weeks later if needed.
- **Short by 5–10%:** That's normal. Run a fourth week mirroring Week 3, then progress.
- **Still fatigued, or regressing:** Pause progression and send him back to his GP. Persistent post-viral fatigue needs medical input, not more training.
